hypothesis: As direct-context length increases, normalized-exact retrieval accuracy may decline when the single target record is embedded naturally among deterministic distractor records with the same registry-entry semantic structure, vocabulary, and access-code format.
null_result: Accuracy may remain stable across the tested ladder; absence of degradation remains valid evidence.
controlled_variables: one unique short access-code answer per case
same record template for target and distractors

case_generation.record_template: Registry entry: Project {entity} has access code {answer}.
case_generation.model_specific_budgeting: Each model receives a deterministic prefix of the same symmetric distractor sequence. The terminal record count may differ because model tokenizers differ; requested and actual counts are retained.

evidence_position.note: The target record is one ordinary registry entry. Its ratio is measured within the registry-entry context, excluding fixed chat-template and question overhead. Symmetric before/after distractor pairs keep position stable across levels.

metrics.reliability_rule: ECC threshold is the last level in the contiguous tested prefix meeting the threshold; a later isolated recovery does not raise ECC.
metrics.right_censoring: If a threshold holds at the largest tested level, report it as a tested lower bound rather than a measured failure boundary.

success_criteria: target and distractor entity/code uniqueness validated before inference
accuracy and descriptive runtime aggregated by context level
ECC thresholds and right-censoring status derived only with complete supporting data
same definition reusable across both qualified models
